subject: Request: temporary retention exception for EU customer logs (Finexa)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finexa.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finexa Support <support@finexa.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: Can you preserve request traces longer than policy for debug?

Hi Hannah,

We're seeing a recurring failure in production where payments for certain Irish customers fail during settlement. Our engineering team has asked if Redwood can hold request traces and KV caches an extra 7 days beyond our current 30-day retention so we can correlate with downstream banking logs.

I attached a small error sample (finexa-error-sample-20261201.log.txt) and a short reproduction note. We understand data residency rules — Finexa is an Irish entity and requests that any extended logging remain in EU regions.

Can Redwood approve a temporary retention extension limited to the affected customer IDs and a strict 7-day window? We'll sign any required exception paperwork and limit access to a named triage team.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Senior SRE, Finexa Payments
liam@finexa.com

On Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:00 GMT, Liam O'Connor wrote: > Forwarding the original trace sample for context.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Can you preserve request traces longer than policy for debug?

Folks — looping you in. Finexa (EU customer) needs a short-term retention extension (requested 7 days) scoped to specific customer IDs to diagnose settlement failures. They explicitly require data to stay in EU.

Quick notes / asks:
- Is 7 days feasible from infra/security side if we scope to specific request IDs and restrict access?
- Do we need a signed exception form + CS/Legal approval before we touch anything?
- If approved, who executes: runtime ops to change retention policy or a support snapshot only?

I've attached the customer's sample log and a draft exception form they said they'd sign.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE (EMEA) — Redwood Inference

Attachment: finexa-error-sample-20261201.log.txt
Attachment: retention-exception-request-form.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-team@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 07:30:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Can you preserve request traces longer than policy for debug?

Thanks Hannah & Liam (copied),

Security/Compliance review: short version = we can support a timeboxed exception if the following controls are in place:
1) Scope: explicit list of request IDs or customer IDs — no blanket tenant-wide policy change.
2) Timebox: maximum 7 days (we can do 72 hours by default; 7 days requires Exec approval).
3) Region lock: data must remain in EU region and we must not copy to any non-EU backup.
4) Access: add named triage group (max 4 people). All access will be logged and reviewed.
5) Paperwork: sign the standard retention-exception-request-form (attached).

Operational considerations:
- We prefer creating an immutable audit snapshot of the affected request traces and storing that snapshot in the customer's EU project bucket for 7 days rather than changing global retention policy. That minimizes blast radius.
- If Finexa insists on live retention extension (affecting KV caches), we need a 48–72 hour engineering maintenance window and explicit SLA around potential performance impact.

Next steps I propose:
1) Finexa confirms the exact request IDs and the narrow list of engineers who need access.
2) They sign the PDF we attached (retention-exception-request-form.pdf).
3) Security will provision a 72-hour EU-bound snapshot and scoped access; if Finexa needs the full 7 days, I'll escalate to Marissa for exec sign-off.

I'll prepare a short Exec note if needed.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@finexa.com>, security-team@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Can you preserve request traces longer than policy for debug?

Approving a 72-hour, EU-only snapshot and scoped access. Reasoning: preserves customer debug needs while keeping exposure minimal.

Actions approved:
- Security to create an immutable snapshot of request traces for the provided request IDs (EU region only) and retain for 72 hours.
- Access limited to the three named Finexa engineers and two Redwood triage engineers (names to be provided by Liam).
- Finexa must return the signed retention-exception-request-form (we'll attach a DocuSign link if they prefer).
- No KV cache retention changes except under a separate engineering change with 48–72 hour maintenance notice.

Neha: please proceed with provisioning and confirm when the snapshot is accessible. Hannah: please get Liam to send the signed form and the exact request IDs.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
